evidence.computation: The two fee calculators are independent integer divisions (amount * fee / 100), and tTransferAmount subtracts both from tAmount, which reproduces the emitted 10361271992408420210 EXACTLY -- see derivation. The measured tax is therefore 1280606650747108115 / 11641878643155528325 of the requested amount, i.e. the exact rational 512242660298843246000/465675145726221133 bps; taxBpsApproxDecimal is a truncated APPROXIMATION of that non-terminating decimal, and computedTaxBps is the rounded nominal 1100 (_taxFee 2 + _liquidityFee 9 == 11%). Note it is NOT exactly 89% of the requested amount: exact 89% is 10361271992408420209.25, and flooring the 2% and 9% fees SEPARATELY under-collects 1/2 + 1/4 == 3/4 of a base unit, which leaves the recipient exactly 3/4 above exact-89% and lands on the integer 10361271992408420210 == ceil(89%). A single floor(tAmount * 89 / 100) would instead discard that remaining 1/4 and yield 10361271992408420209, so the two integer results differ by one. requestedAmount is calldata word 1 of transfer(address,uint256); transferToRecipient is transferLogData decoded, the single emitted Transfer event.

note: EverMars (EVM) is a SafeMoon-style reflection token taking an 11% cut on every transfer (_taxFee=2 reflection + _liquidityFee=9 liquidity/marketing, both live on-chain). IMPORTANT: unlike fBOMB on 8453, the tax is INVISIBLE in Transfer events — the 9% liquidity fee is credited to _rOwned[address(this)] with no event and the 2% reflection is a rate change, so a taxed transfer emits exactly ONE Transfer event carrying the already-net amount. To verify, compare the requested amount in the transfer() calldata against the emitted Transfer value (see evidence.computation); do not look for a second Transfer event. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) EVM as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE — the destination pool receives only 89% of amountSent, so pool.swap(amount0Out, ...) reverts K() because the demanded output assumed the full amountSent; (2) EVM as TERMINAL OUTPUT — no K() revert, but the user receives 89% of the quoted amountOut, silently violating minAmountOut. Real production impact: vfat support report 1bbe7c95 (2026-07-28), a BSC FIL/WBNB zap-in deposit. The router's zap engine picked USDC -> EVM -> WBNB (PancakeV2 pairs 0xe0daefbd4fbcb6dc6700a954121df2b72dff619b and 0xa32f1e8f55eced305414a8bd7a16d2fe42761382) for the WBNB balancing leg. Those two pairs price EVM 4916x apart and the gap has stood for 10+ days precisely because the tax makes it unarbitrable, so constant-product math on their reserves over-quoted WBNB by 4891x. That drove the zap to allocate 99.979% of the input to FIL and 0.021% to WBNB, and the deposit was rejected with 99.96% dust.

note: Thoreum (THOREUM) is a SafeMoon-style reflection token taking a 20% cut on every transfer. Same invisible-tax structure as EverMars above: _takeLiquidity credits _rOwned[address(this)] with no event and _reflectFee only adjusts _rTotal/_tFeeTotal, so a taxed transfer emits exactly ONE Transfer event carrying the already-net amount. Verify by comparing a requested amount against the emitted Transfer value, not by looking for a second Transfer. WATCH THE DIVISOR: this contract divides by 10000 while the EverMars contract divides by 100, so raw _taxFee/_liquidityFee values are not comparable between the two. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) THOREUM as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE — the destination pool receives only 80% of amountSent, so pool.swap(amount0Out, ...) reverts K() because the demanded output assumed the full amountSent; (2) THOREUM as TERMINAL OUTPUT — no K() revert, but the user receives 80% of the quoted amountOut, silently violating minAmountOut. Why it matters for routing: all four of its BSC pools are dead — PancakeV2 THOREUM/WBNB 0xe859b6a32d953a0ece0027c0fc8575571862c0bb (last swap block 99997979), USDT/THOREUM 0x1edde65bbde8a7d88d0d563b8d6b5378b38e4432 (53388353), THOREUM/BUSD 0x6594a90d41ae84fc5615d376ec59838744737bd7 (50282222) and THOREUM/USDC 0x811229adf04be156138a8cdb069f330766b71117 (47490337) — and they price THOREUM 7.38x apart (from $1.91e-05 in the WBNB pool to $1.41e-04 in the USDT pool). That spread persists precisely because the 20% tax makes it unarbitrable, so constant-product math over those stale reserves produces attractive-looking but unexecutable quotes. A 24h audit of vfat-router native zap-in legs (2026-07-30) found THOREUM used as a two-hop routing intermediate 105 times on BSC, the second most frequent unlisted intermediate on that chain, and it accounted for the largest quoted-versus-restricted output gaps observed in that sample (-78% to -85%). Found while auditing the fallout from support report 1bbe7c95.
